text:
Alexandra: hi folks :wave: I'm Alexandra, starting today on Payments. Trying to run `kubectl get pods -n payments` but getting a Forbidden error. Is there a standard place to request namespace access or a quick way to check what I need?

Alexandra: paste of error:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n payments
Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "okta|alexandra@redwood.com" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "payments"
```

Samir: welcome! :wave: quick checks first: run `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n payments`. If it says no, you'll need namespace RBAC. We typically use the self-serve onboarding form unless you need immediate ephemeral access.

Alexandra: ran `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n payments` — it returns `no`. Current-context is `aws-devops`. Where's the self-serve form?

devex-bot: Hi Alexandra — welcome! :tada: File a request at https://intranet.redwood.com/onboarding/kube-access and include: namespace (payments), requested TTL (choose "ephemeral: 7d" for first-week access), access level (view/edit), and your manager. The system auto-creates a ticket and notifies infra.

infra-team: @Alexandra we can do a quicker smoke-grant if you need immediate read-only access. To validate workflow, you can test impersonation with our onboard service account:
```
kubectl auth can-i get pods -n payments --as=system:serviceaccount:infra:dev-onboard-sa
# expected: yes
```
If that returns yes, we can mirror that RoleBinding to your user. Otherwise open the form and include a short justification.

Matthew: I'll be the approver for Payments requests today — ping me the ticket once it's filed and I'll push it through. Default for new hires is viewer for 7 days; escalate to edit only after a short review.

Alexandra: filed request, ticket INC-2025, link: https://tickets.redwood.com/INC-2025 — set TTL to 7d, access viewer. Thanks!

infra-team: thanks — applying RoleBinding now. I'll bind `view` on namespace `payments` to your Okta principal. Should take ~30s.

infra-team: applied RoleBinding and created `rolebinding/payments-onboard-alexandra` (viewer).

Samir: once infra confirms, try `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n payments` again or `kubectl get pods -n payments`.

Alexandra: success!
```
$ kubectl get pods -n payments
NAME                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
charge-processor-5fd7d   1/1     Running   0          12d
payments-api-7c9f8      2/2     Running   1          3d
```
Thanks everyone :pray: much appreciated!

Matthew: :thumbsup: welcome aboard — reach out if you need write access later, we'll do a short review.
